name: Sacral parasympathetic outflow and bladder control
summary: The sacral parasympathetic neurons in the S2–S4 segments of the conus send preganglionic fibers through the pelvic splanchnic nerves to ganglia in the walls of the bladder, rectum and genitals, driving detrusor contraction, rectal emptying and erection. Micturition is a reflex coordinated in the pontine micturition center and released or withheld by the frontal lobes: bladder filling is sensed, the pons switches detrusor contraction on and the sphincter (pudendal, Onuf's nucleus) off, and the cortex decides when. Lesions above the sacral cord give a spastic, small, reflexic bladder with urgency; lesions of the conus, cauda equina or pelvic nerves give a flaccid, large, areflexic bladder with retention and overflow.

anatomy.location: Sacral parasympathetic nucleus in the intermediolateral region of S2–S4 in the conus medullaris; pelvic splanchnic nerves joining the inferior hypogastric plexus; intramural ganglia in the pelvic viscera; pudendal nerve (S2–S4, somatic) to the external sphincters and perineum.

subdivisions.name: Onuf's nucleus (S2–S4, somatic)
subdivisions.note: external urethral and anal sphincters via the pudendal nerve; spared in ALS, lost in multiple system atrophy

subdivisions.name: Sympathetic (T11–L2) via the hypogastric nerves
subdivisions.note: bladder neck closure, ejaculation, relaxation of the detrusor

subdivisions.name: Medial frontal cortex
subdivisions.note: voluntary initiation and inhibition of voiding

function: Emptying of the bladder and rectum, penile and clitoral erection, and, with the sympathetic and somatic components, continence, ejaculation and coordinated voiding.

bestView.label: cord (the sacral outflow lies in the conus at L1–L2, below the MNI volume)
pontine tegmentum: the micturition center lies dorsally near the locus coeruleus

imaging.normalAppearance: Not imaged directly; the sagittal lumbar MRI shows the conus and cauda equina, and cranial MRI shows the medial frontal and pontine regions. Urodynamics classify the bladder dysfunction.

pathology.finding: Mass, disc or infarct at the conus or compressing the sacral roots with an areflexic bladder.
Cervical or thoracic myelopathy with detrusor overactivity and detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia.

pathology.pathology: Normal pressure hydrocephalus / bilateral medial frontal lesions
pathology.finding: Ventriculomegaly or medial frontal lesions with urge incontinence and gait apraxia.

lesionEffects.deficit: Urgency, frequency and reflex incontinence with a small bladder
lesionEffects.mechanism: Suprasacral cord lesion: detrusor overactivity without inhibition, often with dyssynergia

lesionEffects.deficit: Retention with overflow, a large painless bladder, absent anal reflex
lesionEffects.mechanism: Conus, cauda equina or pelvic nerve lesion: detrusor areflexia
Loss of cortical inhibition and awareness

examination: Perianal sensation, anal tone, anal and bulbocavernosus reflexes
Lower limb reflexes and plantars to place the lesion above or below the conus
Gait and cognition if a frontal cause is suspected
pearls: Retention means the lesion is at or below the conus (or spinal shock); urgency means it is above
Preserved sphincter control in a patient with wasted hands and brisk legs favors ALS; early incontinence favors multiple system atrophy
